function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on rural highways, 35 mph on urban highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is illegal for all drivers.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Lower limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority. | | **Headlights & Signals** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or stop sign.
• Parking on a curb is prohibited unless marked. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Towing requires a valid permit and proper equipment. | | **School Bus Rules** | • All vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• The bus’s red lights and stop sign must be active. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on a two‑lane road unless passing. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in some counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Points are added to your driving record for violations.
• Accumulating points can lead to license suspension. | | **Special Rules for Commercial Vehicles** | • Different speed limits, weight restrictions, and licensing requirements. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic statutes. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Offers guides, FAQs, and downloadable handbooks. - **Texas Highway Patrol** – Provides enforcement guidelines and public safety notices. If you need details on a particular rule (e.g., “how many points does a speeding ticket add?”) or want to check the most recent updates, let me know!
